title: Cap. VIII Arg. 1 Resp.: simple complacence vs predestinating will; non-election is not willing to destroy
pass_a_gloss: If the adversaries mean this, that God, foresight and antecedent consideration of human demerits being set aside, wills salvation equally to all men, this we deny can be effected from the places alleged. It is indeed effected that God by the will of simple complacence wills that all believe, that all repent, that no one perish, that no one be damned; but it is not effected that God by predestinating will wills equally, before foresight of demerits, to work in all that they believe, that they repent; to work that they not perish, that they not be damned: nor is it effected that God by reprobating will has not decreed to deny to certain ones efficacious grace, and infallible ordination unto glory. For these two can stand together: God wills that all believe, and no one perish, namely by the will of simple complacence; and, God wills to permit that certain ones persist in their voluntary unbelief, and fall short of eternal salvation. In this therefore the adversaries err, that they take these two, not to elect or to reprobate, and to will to destroy or to inflict eternal death, as equipollent: whereas non-election or passing by can compete unto an intact creature, which is manifest in the angels; but the will of destroying or of affecting with eternal death cannot fall except upon a vitiated creature: since non-election is the mere negation of a gratuitous benefit, Death or perdition is the wage of committed sin. It is indeed most true that all the non-elect will infallibly rush into eternal death: it is also clear that all the non-elect from eternity by the positive will of God are adjudged to this death: but this deputing unto death is not to be conceived as performed in the same sign of reason in which non-election is established, but in another later, in which the final perseverance of the non-elect in the state of sin is foresighted. From this therefore that God wills no one to perish without antecedent consideration of demerits, it does not follow that God wills no one to pass by or not-elect without antecedent consideration of the same.
pass_b_english: If adversaries mean that God, foresight of human demerits set aside, wills salvation equally to all, we deny the cited places prove that. They do prove that by the will of simple complacence God wills that all believe and repent, that none perish or be damned. They do not prove that by predestinating will he wills equally, before foresight of demerits, to work in all so they believe and repent, and not perish or be damned — nor that by reprobating will he has not decreed to deny some efficacious grace and infallible ordination to glory. Those two can stand together: God wills that all believe and none perish (simple complacence); and God wills to permit some to persist in voluntary unbelief and fall short of eternal salvation. Adversaries err in taking not-to-elect (or to reprobate) as equipollent with willing to destroy or inflict eternal death. Non-election or praeterition can fall on an intact creature — plain in the angels — but the will to destroy or afflict with eternal death can fall only on a vitiated creature: non-election is mere denial of a gratuitous benefit; death or perdition is sin's wage. True: all the non-elect will infallibly rush into eternal death, and from eternity God's positive will adjudges them to it — but that deputing to death is not conceived in the same sign of reason as non-election, but in a later one where final perseverance in sin is foresighted. That God wills none to perish without prior regard to demerits does not entail that he wills none to pass by or not-elect without that same prior regard.
source_text: Si id volunt adversarii, Deum seposita praevisione et consideratione antecedente demeritorum humanorum, velle ex aequo salutem universis hominibus, hoc nos negamus ex locis allegatis effici posse. Efficitur quidem, Deum voluntate simplicis complacentiae velle ut omnes credant, ut omnes resipiscant, ut nemo pereat, ut nemo damnetur; sed non efficitur, Deum voluntate praedestinante velle ex aequo, ante praevisionem demeritorum, in omnibus operari ut credant, ut resipiscant; operari ne pereant, ne damnentur: neque efficitur, Deum voluntate reprobante haud decrevisse negare quibusdam gratiam efficacem, et infallibilem ordinationem ad gloriam. Possunt enim haec duo simul consistere: Deus vult ut omnes credant, et nemo pereat, scilicet voluntate simplicis complacentiae; et, Deus vult permittere ut quidam in infidelitate sua voluntaria persistent, et ab aeterna salute deficiant. In eo igitur errant adversarii, quod sumunt haec duo, non-eligere sive reprobare, et velle perdere vel mortem aeternam inferre, pro aequipollentibus: cum non-electio vel praeteritio competere possit in creaturam integram, quod in angelis manifestum est; at voluntas perdendi vel morte aeterna afficiendi non potest cadere nisi in creaturam vitiatam: cum non-electio sit mera negatio gratuiti beneficii, Mors sive perditio sit stipendium commissi peccati. Est quidem verissimum, omnes non-electos infallibiliter ruituros in mortem aeternam: est etiam perspicuum, omnes non-electos ab aeterno positiva Dei voluntate huic morti adjudicatos: sed haec ad mortem deputatio non concipienda est ut in eodem signo rationis peracta, quo non-electio statuitur, sed in alio posteriore, quo non-electi perseverantia finalis in statu peccati praevidetur. Ex eo igitur quod Deus neminem vult perire absque antecedanea consideratione demeritorum, non sequitur, Deum neminem velle praeterire aut non-eligere absque antecedanea consideratione eorundem.
